# Man arrested in arson inside Bothell Fred Meyer store

---

Thu, August 13, 2026 at 9:28 AM

Crews at the scene of the fire inside the Bothell Fred Meyer on Aug. 4, 2026. (Bothell Fire Department)

Bothell police on Thursday arrested a suspect on suspicion of first-degree arson at a Fred Meyer store last week.

On the afternoon of Aug. 4, Bothell Fire Department crews responded to reports of smoke and flames inside the store near Thrasher's Corner.

The fire alarm and sprinkler systems came on, and everyone in the store safely evacuated.

Crews had to ventilate the building.

Through the investigation, Bothell police identified a suspect.

K-9 and drone teams assisted the Bothell Police Department's Investigations Unit and Community Crime Reduction Team with taking the suspect into custody.

CRIME BLOTTER

# Bothell Police arrest arson suspect in Fred Meyer fire near Thrasher’s Corner

Aug 13, 2026, 9:53 AM

Fire crews respond to a fire at the Fred Meyer in Bothell. (Photo courtesy of the Bothell Fire Department)

(Photo courtesy of the Bothell Fire Department)

BY MYNORTHWEST STAFF

  

MyNorthwest.com

Bothell Police arrested a suspect in connection with last week’s fire at the Fred Meyer near Thrasher’s Corner shortly after 7 a.m. this morning.

The suspect faces a first-degree arson charge. Police also said the suspect was found in a stolen vehicle at the time of the arrest.

“This arrest was the result of coordinated work between our Investigations Unit and our Community Crime Reduction Team (CCRT) with support from our K9 and Drone teams,” Bothell Police said in a news release Thursday morning.

The investigation into the Fred Meyer fire continues.

## How the Bothell Fred Meyer fire started

On Aug. 4 at 1:43 p.m., Bothell fire crews were dispatched to Fred Meyer after patrons reported seeing flames and smoke in the building, according to the Bothell Fire Department.

Erin Gowenlock, a spokesperson for the City of Bothell, told KIRO Newsradio the fire originated inside the store near the garden center.

The store’s fire alarm and sprinkler systems activated, and employees and customers safely evacuated. No injuries were reported.

Firefighters extinguished the fire.

“There was smoke throughout the building, and water was concentrated in and around the affected area,” Gowenlock stated.

The cause of the fire is under investigation. No nearby businesses were affected.

Follow @http://twitter.com/Mynorthwest
A Snohomish man is suspected of starting a fire that caused more than $200,000 in damage at a Fred Meyer in Bothell earlier this month.

If You See Something Say Something

On September 11th, 2020, just after 2:00 p.m. 53 year-old Sammy Piatt was arrested by the Oregon City Police Department after he lit a pile of leaves on fire near the Clackamas County Community Solutions building located at 112 11th St. in Oregon City, Oregon.

The investigation started after a Clackamas County Probation officer observed smoke coming from the area of the steps to the Community Solutions building and Mr. Piatt standing near the fire. One probation officer detained Mr. Piatt and another probation officer used a fire extinguisher to quickly extinguish the fire. The fire was approximately ten feet from the building and did not result in any damage to the building.

Mr. Piatt admitted to lighting the leaves on fire. He was arrested without incident for Arson II and on a probation violation. He is currently lodged at the Clackamas County Jail and is transient.

We want to emphasize the importance of; if you see something, say something. If you see something suspicious please call 911 or non-emergency dispatch.

Reference OCPD Case # 20-019510

# Man arrested on arson charge after lighting leaf pile on fire in Oregon City

---

by KATU Staff

Sat, September 12, 2020 at 11:05 PM

Sammy Piatt booking photo courtesy Clackamas County Jail

OREGON CITY, Ore. — Oregon City Police arrested a man Friday afternoon after they say he lit a pile of leaves on fire near the Clackamas County Community Solutions building.

Police said they responded to the incident after a Clackamas County Probation officer saw smoke coming from near the steps to the Community Solutions building and saw the suspect, 53-year-old Sammy Piatt, standing near the fire.

A probation officer detained Piatt and another officer used a fire extinguisher to put out the fire.

Police said the fire was about 10 feet from the building.

Piatt admitted he lit the leaves on fire. He was arrested on charges of second-degree arson and on a probation violation. He was lodged at the Clackamas County Jail.

Police ask the public to call 911 or the non-emergency number if they see any suspicious activity.
